fields.quoted_span: the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
fields.note: Disclosure duty, the ban on non-refundable renewal fees (including roommate-related fees) and the applicability clause are all in the document. The closing sentence that the dollar cap, receipt, credit-report copy and refund rules are state law is a fair reading of the page's references to Civ. Code § 1950.6.

fields.quoted_span:
The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is
$68.96
fields.note: The disclosure and the existing-tenant fee ban are stated. The $68.96 figure appears on the Rent Board page. The page says nothing about a Berkeley-specific dollar cap, but the rule's description of the state maximum matches it.
The rule's effective_date is empty and the document gives no effective date for chapter 13.78.

fields.quoted_span: Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of any contractual language in any rental agreement or lease to the contrary.
fields.note: The page presents the chapter as currently applicable, which is consistent with in_force. It never says so explicitly.

fields.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant
fields.note: The coverage summary matches the page, which states no unit-count, construction-date or Rent Ordinance limits.

fields.quoted_span: Notification of state law limitation on tenant screening fees (BMC 13.78.010)
fields.note: The page names BMC 13.78.010, 13.78.016 and 13.78.018 and lists Municipal Code 13.78 as related, which matches the citation and its aliases.
